$comment: Layer 4 - claims this repository cannot prove on its own: a physical device, the App Store, an external service. Each entry is a dated statement of what a human observed, with an expiry and a re-verify recipe, referenced from a governed document with <!-- vt-claim: attested <id> -->. An entry past its budget FAILS the gate, and so does one no document references. Device and store claims are NOT auto-detected from prose - the marker is how such a claim enters the ledger.

entries.claim: The authenticated gplay CLI cannot read the Play App Signing certificate: no signing/cert command exists, and the sha256 returned by `gplay bundles list` is the digest of the uploaded AAB, not the certificate fingerprint. The SHA-256 for well-known-assetlinks.ts is therefore Console-only, owner-side. Re-verify with `gplay --help` and `gplay bundles --help`; this entry fails the day a certificate read is added, at which point the row becomes an agent step.

entries.claim: The Railway project VetTrack (adf88531-75ce-41a8-9f9f-b27e88c87772) has a single environment, production (63549599-7b9a-4214-aba6-d1b8a9b638bf). On the Worker service, these names are all set: NODE_ENV (= production), DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, DB_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, APNS_KEY_P8, APNS_KEY_ID, APNS_TEAM_ID, APNS_BUNDLE_ID, FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON — the worker's own required set, which is deliberately NOT the API's REQUIRED_IN_PRODUCTION list (that list also names VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and ALLOWED_ORIGIN, which the worker does not need and does not carry) — and the three shared names are defined as exact references: DB_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=${{VetTrack.DB_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED}}, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=${{VetTrack.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID}}, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=${{VetTrack.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}}. On the VetTrack service (551051c2-fcda-47f8-9823-1d95455a5e3e) none of NIXPACKS_NODE_VERSION, ACCESS_KEY_ID, BUCKET, ENDPOINT, REGION, SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, RAILWAY_BUCKET_ID is set and ANDROID_PLAY_SIGNING_SHA256 is. No staged patch is pending. Re-verify with GraphQL, UNRENDERED (the CLI's `variables --json` renders references into literals and cannot tell the two apart), asserting booleans only so no secret value is printed — with T=$(jq -r .user.accessToken ~/.railway/config.json), P=adf88531-75ce-41a8-9f9f-b27e88c87772, E=63549599-7b9a-4214-aba6-d1b8a9b638bf, W=<Worker serviceId from `railway status --json`>, V=551051c2-fcda-47f8-9823-1d95455a5e3e: `curl -s -X POST https://backboard.railway.com/graphql/v2 -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"query\":\"{ envs: project(id:\\\"$P\\\"){ environments { edges { node { name } } } } w: variables(projectId:\\\"$P\\\", environmentId:\\\"$E\\\", serviceId:\\\"$W\\\", unrendered:true) v: variables(projectId:\\\"$P\\\", environmentId:\\\"$E\\\", serviceId:\\\"$V\\\", unrendered:true) s: environmentStagedChanges(environmentId:\\\"$E\\\"){ patch } }\"}" | jq -e '. as $root | (.errors == null) and (.data != null) and ([ (.data.envs.environments.edges | map(.node.name)) == ["production"], (.data.w.NODE_ENV == "production"), (["DATABASE_URL","REDIS_URL","APNS_KEY_P8","APNS_KEY_ID","APNS_TEAM_ID","APNS_BUNDLE_ID","FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON"] | all(. as $n | ($root.data.w | has($n)) and (($root.data.w[$n] | length) > 0))), (.data.w.DB_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED == "${{VetTrack.DB_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED}}"), (.data.w.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID == "${{VetTrack.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID}}"), (.data.w.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY == "${{VetTrack.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}}"), ((.data.w | has("VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY")) | not), (["NIXPACKS_NODE_VERSION","ACCESS_KEY_ID","BUCKET","ENDPOINT","REGION","SECRET_ACCESS_KEY","RAILWAY_BUCKET_ID"] | all(. as $n | ($root.data.v | has($n)) | not)), (.data.v | has("ANDROID_PLAY_SIGNING_SHA256")), ((.data.s == null) or (.data.s.patch == {})) ] | all)'` must exit 0 and print `true`. `jq -e` exits non-zero on `false`, so the check fails closed; a GraphQL error or missing `data` fails on the first two terms rather than being read as "empty". The last term accepts `null` for `s` because after `environmentPatchCommitStaged` Railway has no staged record at all (`describe-environment` reports `staged: null`), which is the desired state — it never treats a missing `patch` inside a present record as empty.
entries.evidence: Railway CLI variable listings (names only) and GraphQL environmentStagedChanges, read by the operations session of 2026-09-10/11

entries.claim: server/lib/well-known-assetlinks.ts builds exactly one statement, for android_app uk.vettrack.app with the handle_all_urls relation, whose sha256_cert_fingerprints set is exactly the UPLOAD_KEY_CERT_FINGERPRINTS list from server/lib/well-known-assetlinks.ts (the Capacitor shell's local upload key 93:34:4C:4B:9F:2D:22:CC:61:DA:0C:35:71:CF:98:E5:85:22:A3:0A:CA:B8:98:17:2A:28:E7:FC:9F:82:5C:83 and the EAS-managed upload key 38:31:8A:51:1A:61:74:CF:F9:0A:BF:3F:8C:4B:AB:DF:B6:9B:34:F4:82:90:3F:C1:A6:F9:9D:FA:8B:A1:4F:5F) plus the value of ANDROID_PLAY_SIGNING_SHA256, the Play App Signing key (C4:17:D1:FA:83:F3:4A:7C:C9:4E:63:14:39:ED:FE:FD:13:F0:B3:2F:D2:BA:D5:65:A8:7C:CC:78:5F:B9:CE:3E). The EAS upload key was measured with `keytool -printcert -jarfile` on the downloaded AAB 10302 and matches Play Console → App integrity → Upload key certificate. LIVE STATE: as attested 2026-09-10 the deployed endpoint serves two of these (93:34 + C4:17); it serves all three only once the change that added 38:31 (vettrack PR #302) is deployed — until then this entry attests the code and the AAB measurement, not the endpoint. Acceptance check to run after that deploy, fail-closed jq: `mapfile -t UP < <(grep -o '[0-9A-F:]\{95\}' server/lib/well-known-assetlinks.ts); PLAY=C4:17:D1:FA:83:F3:4A:7C:C9:4E:63:14:39:ED:FE:FD:13:F0:B3:2F:D2:BA:D5:65:A8:7C:CC:78:5F:B9:CE:3E; test ${#UP[@]} = 2 && curl -s https://vettrack.uk/.well-known/assetlinks.json | jq -e --arg a "${UP[0]}" --arg b "${UP[1]}" --arg play "$PLAY" 'length == 1 and .[0].relation == ["delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls"] and .[0].target.namespace == "android_app" and .[0].target.package_name == "uk.vettrack.app" and (.[0].target.sha256_cert_fingerprints | sort) == ([$a,$b,$play] | sort)'` — exit 0 means the endpoint serves exactly those three; anything else is a regression.
